questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic moves in both directions and both drivers can pass. You may only pass if it is safe and will not hit oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You may drive across a dashed white line:

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross them to change lanes or pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A speed restriction sign:

options.text: Can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
Has a triangular shape.
Is blue with black letters.
Shows a safe speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows a safe speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Speed signs on curves and turns show a recommended safe speed. You should slow down even more in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and get ready to stop.
Must stop and check for traffic before going.
May go through if the road is clear.
May not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May go through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can go through the intersection if it is clear. You can also turn left or right unless a sign says not to. Always yield to other cars and people in the intersection.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you must:

options.text: Drive slowly so approaching vehicles and pedestrians can get out of your way.
Honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know you are coming.
Stop and look both ways before entering the street.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look both ways before entering the street.
questions.explanation: Always stop at the edge of the driveway before entering the street. Wait until no pedestrians or cars are coming before you drive out. You must follow this rule.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which signal?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green left arrow gives you the right-of-way. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get ahead of other traffic.
Go slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to the same speed as traffic. Signal, find an opening, and merge into traffic safely.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Stop in the middle of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles with lights and sirens. Move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, go through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: If you notice a problem with your vehicle that affects safety, you should:

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have money.
Drive slower.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any safety problem with your vehicle right away, before you drive it.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Stares at things off the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while talking during driving.
Only watches the car ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for things in your car, daydreaming, or looking at the scenery. Keep checking the road, your mirrors, and your dashboard. These habits will help you stay alert.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving compared to other factors?

options.text: The same way alcohol does.
The same way amphetamines do.
The same way anger does.
The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way alcohol does.
questions.explanation: Lack of sleep and alcohol affect your driving ability in similar ways. Being awake for 18 hours impairs your driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours straight affects your driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: What should you do when another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce your speed to let them pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, move to the right lane if possible. If there is no right lane, wait for the road ahead to clear and then slowly reduce your speed. This lets them pass safely. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the chance of being hit from behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
Curves are ahead.
A hill is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You cannot exit the freeway.
You can either continue or exit from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue ahead.
You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign on a yellow panel means your lane will not continue through the interchange. Instead, it will exit onto a ramp. If you are in this lane, you must either change lanes to continue through or take the exit.

questions.question: What should you do with your lights at dusk or on overcast days?

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Use your parking lights.
Do not use any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of oncoming traffic and within 500 feet of the vehicle ahead. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an animal on the road?

options.text: No special action is needed.
Honk your horn.
Pass the animal as closely as possible.
Drive very carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive very carefully.
questions.explanation: Always be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid startling or scaring it.

questions.question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying, what should you do?

options.text: Drive normally; your emotions will not affect your driving.
Drive faster because you are more alert.
Take time to calm down and focus before you start driving.
Call a friend to talk while you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take time to calm down and focus before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can hurt your ability to drive safely. When you are worried, angry, or upset, your mind is distracted from driving. Calm down and get focused before you start your engine.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in rain?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in the rain.

questions.question: When you meet an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, what must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road space.
Tell them to pull over to make room.
Use high beam headlights so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road space.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, both vehicles must have enough space. Give oncoming traffic at least half of the main road so both drivers can pass safely.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It can cause hearing loss.
It pollutes the air.
It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
It causes poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes exhaust gas from your vehicle and keeps fumes out of the passenger area. A leak can allow carbon monoxide to enter your car. Fix any leaks in your exhaust system right away.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Press your brakes hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Use your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, release the gas pedal to slow down on a slippery road. If you need to slow down more, gently press your brake pedal with steady pressure.

questions.question: A funeral procession is crossing an intersection where you are stopped. What should you do?

options.text: The procession should yield to you.
Let the procession pass after the lead vehicle enters the intersection.
Try to drive through before the lead vehicle reaches you.
Join the procession to cross the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the procession pass after the lead vehicle enters the intersection.
questions.explanation: It is courteous to let a funeral procession pass. Once the lead vehicle enters the intersection, the rest of the procession has the right-of-way. Let them all pass and do not cut into the line.

questions.question: What can reduce a person's ability to drive safely?

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
Not getting enough sleep.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires good physical condition. Alcohol, medications, drugs, and tiredness can all reduce your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the light turns from green to yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the light turns red.
Brake hard to stop quickly.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Be ready to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
